raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent silent parameter corruption when moving FSDP2 models to CPU with uneven parameter shards.

I identified this issue while debugging Qwen3-Omni training and evaluation failures reported in:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/660
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8039

The observed symptoms included degraded evaluation accuracy in multi-node training. The investigation traced the problem to parameter values changing during CPU offloading, without any forward pass, backward pass, or optimizer update.

This PR uses blocking device-to-CPU transfers in both affected verl paths:

- Runtime offloading through `offload_fsdp2_model_to_cpu`.
- Initialization-time offloading inside `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict`, which reuses the same helper.

This follows the discussion in:
https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/741#issuecomment-6139999835

### Root Cause

`model.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` can leave a device-to-CPU transfer in progress while FSDP2 processes the converted parameter.

For uneven shards, `FSDPModule._apply` calls `FSDPParam.reset_sharded_param`, which may allocate new padded CPU storage and copy the transferred local tensor into it. This CPU copy can read the transfer destination before the asynchronous D2H transfer has completed.

Incorrect values can then persist in the new padded storage. Synchronizing after the entire `model.to()` call returns does not repair values that have already been copied into that storage.

This is not specific to NPU: I reproduced the same failure on CUDA by queuing additional computation before the transfer.

### Design & Code Changes

- Use `model.to("cpu", non_blocking=False)` in `offload_fsdp2_model_to_cpu`, so each transfer completes before FSDP2 can consume its CPU result.
- Route the CPU move in `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict` through that helper with `empty_cache=False`, preserving the initialization path's cache behavior.
- Keep the CPU-to-device helper's `non_blocking=True` argument.
- Update transfer-policy tests to require blocking D2H on both CUDA and NPU.
- Generalize the NPU regression into `test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py`, shared by CUDA and NPU CI. It covers nested FSDP2 modules, large even/uneven weights, and the original small bias vectors.
- Queue warmed-up matrix multiplications on the actual conversion stream and check both default and non-default streams. Change parameter values between trials and check CPU values after synchronization to distinguish persistent corruption from an unfinished transfer.
- Update the CUDA regression so it validates parameter correctness rather than requiring the pinned allocation associated with the previous non-blocking D2H path.

The fix uses existing PyTorch module conversion behavior and does not patch private FSDP2 internals or introduce backend-specific synchronization code.

### Related Work

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7347 enabled non-blocking runtime FSDP2 model transfers for performance. This PR changes the D2H policy to restore correctness. The initialization-time asynchronous CPU move predates #7347 and is covered here as well.
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8057 addresses pinned-memory allocation configuration. It does not establish transfer completion before FSDP2 reads CPU data.
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/741 provides a downstream workaround. This PR addresses the shared verl helpers used by downstream callers.

### Validation

#### Investigation and downstream validation

The standalone reproducer uses two accelerator processes and a nested FSDP2 model with either evenly or unevenly sharded weights. It writes known parameter values, saves an independent blocking CPU reference, and checks exact equality after offloading.

No forward pass, backward pass, or optimizer update is involved.

| Environment | Configuration | Uneven shards: asynchronous D2H followed by synchronization | Other cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NPU: PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6 | 10 iterations, no additional queued computation | 10/20 rank-trials failed | All passed |
| CUDA: PyTorch 2.11.0, CUDA 13.0 | 50 iterations, 64 queued matrix multiplications before each transfer | 50/100 rank-trials failed | All passed |

The other cases include evenly sharded controls, blocking D2H transfers, and waiting immediately after each individual D2H conversion. Comparisons use `rtol=0` and `atol=0`.

These are aggregate rank-trial counts; they do not establish that every failure occurred on the same rank.

I also verified that the downstream fix resolves the reported issues and allows two-node Qwen3-Omni training to run successfully. The downstream tests and pre-commit checks passed.

These results establish the failure mechanism and validate the downstream workaround. They are separate from validation of the final changes in this verl PR.

#### Regression coverage

The relevant tests cover:

- Transfer policy for runtime and initialization-time CPU offloading.
- Cache-release behavior and buffer placement during initialization.
- Nested FSDP2 modules with even and uneven shards.
- Exact CPU parameter values and device round-trip correctness.
- Queued computation before runtime offloading on default and non-default streams.
- Per-rank failure reporting after the critical transfer window.

The updated CPU transfer-policy tests were run against the previous NPU-only implementation and the revised implementation:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/utils/test_fsdp2_model_transfer_on_cpu.py -k 'not sharded_save'
```

- Before: 4 failed, 9 passed, 1 deselected. All four failures were CUDA D2H policy checks, covering runtime offloading and initialization on both ranks.
- After: 13 passed, 1 deselected.
- The deselected test is the existing two-process CPU snapshot test, which checks a separate save-to-CPU helper.

These tests verify transfer policy and control flow using mocked device transfers. They ran with PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu and imported `verl.utils.fsdp_utils` from the modified checkout. Accelerator numerical correctness is covered by the distributed regressions listed below.

Ruff lint and formatting, Python syntax, workflow YAML parsing, license checks, device-API checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

I ran the revised numerical regression on a single node with two NPUs. It passed for both default and non-default streams:
```bash
env -u DIST_INIT_METHOD \
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PYTHONPATH" \
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  torchrun \
    --nnodes=1 \
    --node_rank=0 \
    --nproc-per-node=2 \
    --rdzv_backend=static \
    --master_addr=127.0.0.1 \
    --master_port=29517 \
    tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py
```
Result:
```text
FSDP2 npu CPU offload passed: 2 ranks, default and non-default streams
```
This run verified initialization-time offloading, nested FSDP2 modules with even and uneven shards, repeated runtime offloading with queued computation, and exact parameter values on CPU and after restoring to NPU (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`).

Pre-commit checks also passed for this revision.

### Performance Considerations

This change prioritizes parameter correctness over asynchronous D2H overlap.

Blocking D2H can increase host-side waiting and may change whether the resulting CPU storage is pinned. Consequently, keeping `non_blocking=True` in the CPU-to-device helper does not guarantee the same H2D overlap or throughput as before.

The performance impact of this broader verl change has not been quantified. The successful downstream training runs are correctness evidence, not a controlled performance comparison.

### API and Usage

No public API or configuration changes are required.

Existing callers of the two affected helpers automatically receive the corrected D2H behavior.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Read the contribution guide.
- [x] Search for related PRs:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+FSDP2+offload
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+repadding
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+non_blocking
- [x] Continue the existing PR #8187 rather than opening a duplicate.
- [x] Follow the required PR title format.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Review every changed line in the final revision.
- [x] Run pre-commit checks on the final revision.
- [x] Verify the targeted CPU transfer-policy tests, including failures before the change.
- [x] Complete the existing two-process CPU snapshot test.
- [x] Verify the NPU numerical regression.
- [x] Include the shared numerical regression in both CUDA and NPU CI entry points.
- [x] No user-facing API or configuration documentation changes are needed.
- [x] This PR does not modify the `recipe` submodule.
- [x] Request CI through the project's contribution process.

### AI Assistance Disclosure

I used OpenAI Codex to assist with the investigation, implementation, tests, and PR description. I am responsible for reviewing the changes and validating their behavior.

+# limitations under the License.
+
+"""Check FSDP2 CPU offloading on CUDA and NPU, without external model weights.
+
+Launch from the repository root on two or more accelerators:
+    PYTHONPATH=. torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 \
+        tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py
+
+The uneven vectors require CPU repadding even with two ranks. With 32 ranks,
+their length is 4304, reproducing the 135-element shards and 119-element tail
+from the Qwen3-Omni vision bias failure. Evenly sharded vectors are controls.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+from torch.distributed import init_device_mesh
+
+from verl.utils.device import get_device_id, get_device_name, get_torch_device
+from verl.utils.distributed import initialize_global_process_group
+from verl.utils.fsdp_utils import (
+    CPUOffloadPolicy,
+    fsdp2_load_full_state_dict,
+    fully_shard,
+    load_fsdp_model_to_gpu,
+    offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu,
+)
+
+
+def _build_model(mesh):
+    world_size = mesh.size()
+    lengths = {"uneven": world_size * 135 - world_size // 2, "even": world_size * 135}
+    model = torch.nn.Sequential()
+    expected = {}
+    # Put large shards first so small preceding transfers cannot drain the queued
+    # work before the uneven D2H copy. On two ranks these have 4+3 and 4+4 rows.
+    for index, rows in enumerate((world_size * 4 - 1, world_size * 4)):
+        layer = torch.nn.Linear(262144, rows, bias=False, device=get_device_id())
+        value = torch.full((rows, 262144), (index + 1) / 8, dtype=layer.weight.dtype)
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            layer.weight.copy_(value)
+        expected[f"{len(model)}.weight"] = value
+        fully_shard(layer, mesh=mesh)
+        model.append(layer)
+    for index in range(27):
+        layer = torch.nn.Module()
+        for name, length in lengths.items():
+            # Exactly representable BF16 values, distinct across layers and positions.
+            value = ((torch.arange(length) + index) % 127 + 1).to(torch.bfloat16) / 128
+            expected[f"{len(model)}.{name}"] = value
+            layer.register_parameter(name, torch.nn.Parameter(value.to(get_device_id())))
+        fully_shard(layer, mesh=mesh)
+        model.append(layer)
+    fully_shard(model, mesh=mesh)
+    return model, expected
+
+
+def _check_parameters(model, expected, phase, *, full=False):
+    rank, world_size = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
+    failures = []
+    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
+        if full:
+            # Every rank must finish the collectives, even if an earlier parameter differs.
+            actual = param.full_tensor().cpu()
+            reference = expected[name]
+        else:
